summary.text: A 27-year-old unmarried woman presented with infrequent cycles that occurred only after taking withdrawal treatment for menstruation for the last 11 years. She had attained menarche at age 14 years with regular 28–30 day cycles for the next 2 years and a non-significant family history. She was diagnosed with hypothyroidism and started on thyroid replacement therapy.

Examination showed average build, body mass index 21 kg/m^(2), no pallor, galactorrhoea from both sides, well-developed secondary sex characteristics, normal systemic, per-abdominal and external genitalia findings, and an intact hymen. Ultrasonography showed a uterus of 59.3 mm × 15.3 mm × 10.9 mm and normal other organs; MRI showed a small uterus, an 11 mm × 8 mm lesion of the left pons suggestive of cavernous angioma, and mild pituitary hyperplasia.

Hormonal profile showed serum FSH 115.70 mIU/mL (elevated), oestradiol 12.87 pg/mL and anti-Mullerian hormone 0.01 ng/mL (low), with LH 27.22 mIU/mL, prolactin 12.01 ng/mL and TSH 1.57 µIU/mL. The FMR1 premutation study showed no abnormality and karyotype was 46 XX, Inv(9) p12 q13. The case is reported as premature ovarian insufficiency with hypothyroidism, Inv(9) and an asymptomatic solitary cavernous angioma.

The patient and her parents were counselled about the condition, potential complications of hypoestrogenemia and future fertility issues, and the treatment options, including hormone therapy until the age of natural menopause, and options for future childbearing were explained. A neurosurgery opinion was sought for the MRI finding, and she was advised to avoid any active intervention and follow-up.
